findings.finding: When run_manager() or any step of launch_manager raises, the handler updates pipeline_state to blocked and logs, but never calls transition_task(), so dev_tasks.status stays 'coding' (set at line 500). launch_coder (line 1047) and launch_planning_pipeline (lines 271-277) both do the transition correctly. restart_task refuses tasks in (planning, coding, testing) with 409, so a stuck task has no self-service recovery. The exception path also skips preserve_worktree (which the normal blocked path calls at line 600).
findings.evidence: agents.py:615-619: 'except Exception as e: ... await update_pipeline_state(db2, task_id, "blocked"); await append_log(db2, task_id, "pipeline_error", f"Manager failed: {e}")' — no transition_task. Compare agents.py:1047 'await transition_task(db2, task_id, "blocked")' and agents.py:272-273 'await update_pipeline_state(db2, task_id, "blocked"); await transition_task(db2, task_id, "blocked")'.
findings.production_impact: Any unexpected exception during full-pipeline coding leaves the task permanently in 'coding', UI stale, restart returns 409; worktree not preserved. Requires manual DB intervention.
findings.recommendation: In the except block, call update_pipeline_state + transition_task(db2, task_id, 'blocked') inside a try/except (TransitionError, ValueError) guard (copy agents.py:271-277), and call preserve_worktree(task_id) before the alert.

findings.finding: Simple-mode cost estimates use hardcoded constants 0.0000008/0.000004 ('Haiku-era' comment) while coder agents run claude-sonnet-5 (config.py:32-34) and the configured rates are 0.000003/0.000015 (config.py:192-201). Recorded cost_estimate is ~3.75x understated. Full mode computes correctly via compute_actual_cost_usd using settings (manager.py:246-248). Constants bypass config entirely.
findings.evidence: agents.py:33-34 '_COST_PER_INPUT_TOKEN = 0.0000008' / '_COST_PER_OUTPUT_TOKEN = 0.000004'; agents.py:960 'cost = _estimate_cost(tokens_in, tokens_out)'; manager.py:246-248 'cost: float = tokens_in * settings.cost_per_input_token + tokens_out * (settings.cost_per_output_token)'; config.py:193 'default=0.000003'.
findings.production_impact: agent_runs.cost_estimate and all cost dashboards/aggregates understate real simple-mode spend by ~3.75x; cost/budget decisions are wrong while real money is spent at full rate.
findings.recommendation: Remove the two constants; make _estimate_cost read get_settings().cost_per_input_token/cost_per_output_token (or reuse manager.compute_actual_cost_usd).

findings.finding: Both agents have role files, agent_models.json entries (lines 94,98), tests, and auto-register at startup via ensure_all_agents_registered (capability_registry.py:158-181; main.py:1489-1491). But no code statically calls their run functions; their capabilities ('prompt_engineering', 'ui_ux_design', 'design_system_review') are requested nowhere — the manager only ever requests 'frontend_development'/'backend_development' (manager.py:392-397); and the frontend never calls /api/specialized-agents (zero references). Only theoretical path: raw POST /api/specialized-agents/dispatch with the exact capability string.
findings.evidence: manager.py:392-396: 'required_capability = ("frontend_development" if subtask_type == "frontend" else "backend_development")'; prompt_engineer_agent.py:238 'capabilities=["prompt_engineering"]'; ux_design_agent.py:224 'capabilities=["ui_ux_design", "design_system_review"]'; repo-wide grep for those capability strings outside the two files: 0 hits; grep 'specialized' in apps/web: one stale comment only (roadmap/page.tsx:20).
findings.production_impact: Two advertised capabilities cannot be exercised by any product surface; silent dead weight likely to drift; capability coverage claims are misleading.
findings.recommendation: Either wire them to a real entry point (subtask-type mapping or a /agents UI button calling /{name}/run), or mark API-only in roster docs; add a smoke test that every registered capability is requestable somewhere.

findings.finding: AST scan of 345 modules found 28 import cycles (e.g. db.repository -> security.credential_vault -> fleet.audit_log -> fleet.fleet_events -> event_bus.bus -> db.repository; the tools/delegate/delegation family). Three cycles spot-verified to be broken by lazy function-level imports; app boots and mypy passes (497 files), so none are runtime-breaking today. Latent fragility under refactoring.
findings.evidence: Scan: 345 modules analyzed, 28 cycles. repository.py top-level app imports = lines 14-15 only (app.config, app.db.models); credential_vault.py top-level app imports = none.
findings.production_impact: None today; any refactor promoting a lazy import to module level can create a real circular-import startup failure.
findings.recommendation: Add import-linter forbidden-contract CI check or an AST test; document the 28-cycle list in one place.

findings.finding: launch_coder (agents.py:886) and launch_planner (agents.py:695) create AgentRun rows with heartbeats; launch_manager creates none anywhere (grep: zero create_agent_run/finish_agent_run in agents.py manager section and in manager.py). The manager/phasing loop is invisible to run metrics, heartbeat monitoring and orphan recovery.
findings.evidence: agents.py:886 'run = await create_agent_run(db, task_id, run_label, settings.model_coder)'; grep -n 'create_agent_run|finish_agent_run' app/agents/manager.py -> empty.
findings.production_impact: Manager-phase time not attributed in agent runs; no heartbeat exists for a hung manager loop between dispatches (only its sub-agents' own heartbeats).
findings.recommendation: Decide explicitly: add a lightweight AgentRun row around launch_manager, or document intentional exclusion.
